headline: PLS crashes 8% on the ASX today while the NRL Grand Final delivered a thriller — Roosters edge Knights 19-18 in the closest finish of the year.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara took a nasty hit today, dropping 8% to $2.62. No specific news catalyst in the feed, but lithium stocks have been under sustained pressure as global EV demand growth slows and lithium prices remain depressed. The long-term thesis for Pilbara depends on a lithium price recovery — that story hasn't changed, but the wait continues.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slipped about 2% in last night's US session. No specific news out on the company — the broader NASDAQ dipped slightly and growth/gaming stocks felt the pull. The long-term GTA VI catalyst remains the big driver for this stock; short-term wobbles are noise.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: The AI ETF edged down 1.35% today on the ASX, tracking weakness in US tech from last night's session. GOOG — one of its key holdings — fell over 1% as investors debated the pace of returns on massive AI spending. Still down nearly 15% from where you bought in, but AI infrastructure spending is accelerating globally, which is the long-term driver.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Emerging markets slipped about 1% today. Rising oil prices and Middle East tension tend to weigh on developing economies that are net energy importers. Nothing structural — just global risk-off sentiment on the day.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Despite Alphabet reporting a massive 82% jump in Cloud revenue, the stock fell about 1% last night. Investors are focused on the pace of returns from Google's enormous AI infrastructure spending — essentially asking 'when does all this investment start paying off properly?' The underlying business is strong; market mood is just impatient.

movers.name: DHHF ETF
movers.note: DHHF dipped a very modest 0.39% today — essentially flat. As a broadly diversified ETF, it's doing exactly what it should: smoothing out the bumps. Nothing to worry about here.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS edged down 0.47% today on the ASX, reflecting last night's mild S&P 500 dip of 0.52%. The US market is digesting a busy earnings week and rising oil prices. Still in the green overall for your position — sit tight.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG was basically flat today, down just 0.13%. The diversified nature of this fund means single-day noise barely registers. Long-term story is intact.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft was the standout last night, gaining 0.66% while most of the market slipped. The market is rewarding Microsoft's Azure cloud growth and confidence that its AI spending (a $50 billion bet on Azure expansion) will pay off faster than rivals. Earnings are due this week — worth watching.

watch_today.title: Pilbara Minerals — brutal 8% drop today
watch_today.detail: PLS fell 8% today to $2.62, and you're now down over 61% on this position. That's a painful number. But lithium's slump is industry-wide — this isn't a Pilbara-specific collapse. If you still believe in the long-term EV/battery storage story, this is a hold (or even a top-up consideration if you have conviction). The thesis is bruised, not broken. Only sell if you've genuinely lost faith in the lithium cycle recovering.

watch_today.title: Microsoft earnings due this week — your best performer
watch_today.detail: MSFT reports earnings this week (US time). You're up 18% on this position and it rose another 0.66% last night. Azure cloud growth and AI momentum are the story. A strong result could push it higher; any disappointment could cause a short-term dip. For a long-term holder, either way you sit tight — but it's worth knowing the number is coming.

watch_today.title: Google Cloud up 82% — but stock still dipped
watch_today.detail: Alphabet reported a stunning 82% jump in Cloud revenue, yet the stock fell 1% last night because Wall Street is fixated on how quickly the massive AI capex (capital expenditure — money being poured into data centres and chips) will translate to profit. Your GOOG position is still up 3.2% overall. The business is genuinely strong — this is a hold and a reassurance.

watch_today.title: Oil spiked 3.8% — watch the inflation ripple
watch_today.detail: Crude oil jumped nearly 4% last night to over $103 a barrel. That's a meaningful move. Reports that Iran has detailed plans to target Gulf undersea infrastructure if conflict escalates are rattling energy markets. Higher oil feeds into inflation, which could slow the pace of interest rate cuts globally. Keep an eye on this — it affects everything from your ETFs to the Aussie economy.

watch_today.title: GXAI — down again, still a long-term bet
watch_today.detail: Your AI ETF dipped another 1.35% today and is sitting 14.86% below your entry price. The short-term pain is real, but global AI infrastructure spending is genuinely accelerating — the companies inside this ETF (including Google, Microsoft, Nvidia) are at the centre of that. If you bought this as a 5+ year theme, the story hasn't changed. Hold.

watch_today.title: Take-Two — GTA VI still the long game
watch_today.detail: TTWO slipped ~2% last night with no specific news. You're down 5.64% on this position. The entire thesis for this stock is GTA VI — when it drops, it's expected to be one of the biggest entertainment launches in history. Nothing has changed on that front. This is a hold and wait.

world.summary: Middle East tensions are escalating fast, with Iran increasingly in focus. US midterm politics are heating up with Obama back on the trail, and global economic resilience is being questioned heading into 2027.

stories.title: Trump preparing for Iran escalation — and Iran is stepping up threats
stories.why_it_matters: Multiple reports this weekend paint a concerning picture around the US and Iran. Bloomberg reports the Trump administration is actively preparing for possible military escalation against Iran after elections wrap up. At the same time, US intelligence officials are warning that Iran is trying harder than ever to target American personnel in the Middle East. Perhaps most alarming: Reuters reports Iran has detailed contingency plans to attack undersea internet and energy cables in the Gulf if war resumes — which could knock out communications and energy infrastructure across the region. Oil jumped nearly 4% last night partly on these fears. Any actual conflict would send energy prices soaring and rattle global markets.

stories.title: Iran reportedly plans to attack Gulf undersea cables if war breaks out
stories.why_it_matters: US officials have told Reuters that Iran holds detailed plans to sabotage undersea fibre-optic and energy cables running through the Gulf if a new war breaks out. These cables carry internet traffic and energy data for much of the Middle East and connect to global networks. Cutting them wouldn't just be symbolic — it could disrupt banking, communications and oil trading across the region. This kind of infrastructure warfare threat is a new and serious dimension to the Iran standoff.

stories.title: Obama hits the campaign trail ahead of US midterm elections
stories.why_it_matters: Barack Obama is back out on the campaign trail, stumping for Democratic candidates ahead of the US midterm elections. Midterms will determine who controls Congress, which in turn shapes what Trump can and can't do in the second half of his term — including on tariffs, tax policy, and foreign policy. A Democratic Congress would act as a significant brake on Trump's agenda. For Australian investors, a shift in US political balance affects global trade and market sentiment.

stories.title: Trump administration sues to block potential Democratic win in Alaska
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has launched a lawsuit aimed at blocking a voting method in Alaska that analysts say could favour a Democratic candidate. Alaska uses a ranked-choice voting system in some races, and the legal challenge is widely seen as an attempt to tilt the playing field ahead of midterms. It's part of a broader pattern of pre-election legal battles that are adding uncertainty to the US political outlook.

stories.title: Global economic resilience under strain — analysts warn of policy crossroads
stories.why_it_matters: A new analysis warns that the global economy's ability to absorb shocks is being stretched thin — rising oil prices, US-Iran tensions, sticky inflation in Western economies, and slowing growth in China are all piling on at once. The report calls for decisive policy action from central banks and governments, suggesting the window to act without major damage is narrowing. For Australian investors, this matters because a global slowdown hits commodity exports, company earnings, and your ETF values.

politics.summary: No Australian domestic political news came through in today's feeds. The political radar is quiet locally.

stories.title: No Australian political news today
stories.why_it_matters: Nothing significant broke in Australian domestic politics today. The feeds were quiet on this front. We'll pick it back up tomorrow if anything develops.

ai.summary: This weekend's AI conversation is dominated by regulation — governments around the world are racing to catch up with AI development, while the debate about how to actually control powerful AI systems heats up.

stories.title: The 'kill switch' debate: experts say it's the wrong frame for AI safety
stories.why_it_matters: The idea of an AI 'kill switch' — a button you press to shut the whole thing down — has become popular in AI safety debates, but experts are increasingly saying it misses the point. The real challenge isn't having an off switch; it's building AI systems that are aligned with human values from the ground up, so you never need one. This debate matters because it shapes how governments and companies approach AI safety rules — and those rules will affect every AI-powered product you use.

stories.title: US tech leaders push for AI rules — China already has them
stories.why_it_matters: American tech CEOs are urgently calling on Washington to set clear rules for AI development — but China already has a functioning regulatory framework in place. This is a striking reversal of the usual narrative where Western companies resist regulation. The argument being made is that without rules, AI development becomes a wild west that nobody wins. For investors in AI-exposed stocks like GOOG, MSFT, and GXAI, clear regulation could actually be a long-term positive — it creates a stable operating environment and raises barriers for smaller competitors.

stories.title: India plans its own AI law as risks grow
stories.why_it_matters: India's technology minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has announced that India is working on its own AI law to manage the risks of rapidly advancing AI systems. With over 1.4 billion people and a massive and growing tech sector, India's regulatory choices will shape how global AI companies operate in one of the world's biggest markets. This adds to the picture of a world moving — slowly but unmistakably — toward AI governance frameworks.

stories.title: Query ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini simultaneously — new tool for $29.97
stories.why_it_matters: A new app lets you type one question and get simultaneous answers from ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini side-by-side — available for a one-off $29.97 with a discount code. In practical terms, this means you can compare how different AI models approach the same problem without switching between tabs. Useful for anyone using AI for work, research, or writing — you can see at a glance which model gives you the most useful answer.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 barely moved today — up just 0.02%, essentially flat. Last night in the US, the S&P 500 dipped 0.52% and the NASDAQ fell 0.21% as investors weighed a busy earnings season against rising oil prices. The big commodity story is crude oil surging nearly 4% to over $103 a barrel on Middle East tensions involving Iran. Gold pulled back 1.3% after recent strong gains. The Aussie dollar nudged up slightly to 70.4 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Essentially flat today — the local market shrugged off last night's mild US weakness.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session saw a modest pullback as earnings optimism was offset by rising oil and Middle East tension.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech held up better than the broader market last night despite GOOG dipping on AI spending concerns.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil surged nearly 4% last night — the biggest single-session move in months — driven by Iran escalation fears and reports of plans to target Gulf energy infrastructure.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold pulled back after recent highs, though it remains above $4,000 — a level that would have seemed extraordinary a few years ago.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar edged slightly higher — near 70.4 US cents. A stronger AUD marginally reduces the value of your US holdings when converted back.

sport.summary: It's been a huge weekend of rugby league with the Rugby League World Cup in full swing, the NRL Grand Final result is in, and there's sad AFL news with the death of a former Port Adelaide player.

stories.title: Roosters win NRL Grand Final 19-18 over Knights in a classic
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters claimed the 2026 NRL Premiership with a heart-stopping 19-18 win over the Newcastle Knights at Accor Stadium. One point separated the two sides at full time — it doesn't get closer than that. The Knights had a chance to win it right at the end but the Roosters held on. An absolutely incredible Grand Final for the neutral.

stories.title: Samoa smash PNG thanks to Leniu's dominant performance
stories.why_it_matters: Samoa put in a dominant display against Papua New Guinea in the Rugby League World Cup, with Roosters prop Spencer Leniu the standout. PNG were outclassed, leaving their World Cup campaign in serious trouble. Samoa look like genuine contenders this tournament.

stories.title: England hammer France — Brimson leads record rout
stories.why_it_matters: England put France to the sword in a record-breaking World Cup win, with Warrington winger Matty Brimson starring in the rout. The margin of victory set a new England World Cup record. England are shaping up as one of the tournament's powerhouses.

stories.title: Jillaroos star's World Cup ends in heartbreak with serious injury
stories.why_it_matters: A Jillaroos (Australian women's rugby league) star has suffered a serious injury that has ended her Women's Rugby League World Cup campaign. The injury occurred during the tournament and was described as an 'awful sight' by witnesses. A devastating blow for the player and the Australian women's team.

stories.title: Former Port Adelaide AFL player Daniel Stewart dies suddenly, aged 37
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL world is mourning the sudden death of former Port Adelaide player Daniel Stewart, who has passed away at just 37 years old. Stewart played for the Power and his death has shocked the footy community. No further details about the circumstances have been released. Our thoughts go out to his family, friends, and former teammates.
